title: Oil Price Hits Wartime High Above $120 a Barrel as Iran War Standoff Continues
partialText: The longer the disruption to Middle East fuel supplies lasts, the risk grows that higher energy costs will feed into broader inflation that could dent economic growth.

title: U.S. Economy Grew 2 Percent in Early 2026 Even as War in Iran Began to Hit Energy Prices
partialText: Gross domestic product expanded at a 2 percent annual rate in the first three months of the year, a period including first weeks of conflict in the Middle East.

title: Why the U.A.E. Is Quitting OPEC
partialText: The United Arab Emirates is walking away from OPEC this May. The New York Times’ energy reporter, Rebecca Elliott, breaks down how the war with Iran provided the perfect opening for the Emirates to go solo.

title: Behind Powell’s High-Stakes Decision to Stay at the Fed
partialText: Jerome H. Powell will remain a governor at the Federal Reserve after his term as chair ends, in a bid to guard against a further incursion by the Trump administration on the central bank’s independence.

title: Rising Fuel Prices Force Policymakers to Weigh Excruciating Choices
partialText: The Bank of England and European Central Bank held interest rates steady on Thursday, as officials search for signs of possible longer-term damage and warn of the impact of a prolonged energy shock.

title: After Supreme Court Decision, Louisiana Weighs Redrawing House Maps
partialText: It was not immediately clear whether Gov. Jeff Landry, a Republican, would postpone the May 16 primary election for House races after the court ruled the state’s congressional districts unconstitutional.

title: In Blow to Voting Rights Act, Supreme Court Embraces Claim of Racial Progress
partialText: The majority said the law was a victim of its own success and no longer needed. Dissenters responded that Congress should make the call.

title: Some Black Southerners Say Voting Rights Ruling ‘Missed the Mark’
partialText: Veterans of the civil rights movement and others said the Supreme Court decision felt like a bleak end to decades of gains in Black representation in the region.

title: Chief Justice Roberts Played the Long Game on Voting Rights
partialText: Since his early days as a lawyer and in his first years on the bench, the chief justice has worked to limit the force of the Voting Rights Act.

title: Gov. Janet Mills Exits Maine Senate Race as an Insurgent Democrat Rises
partialText: Her withdrawal reflects the energy of the party’s left and voters’ unease with older candidates and paves the way for Graham Platner to challenge Senator Susan Collins in November.

title: ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ Review: A Rhapsody in Cerulean
partialText: In this sequel, Andy (Anne Hathaway) and Miranda (Meryl Streep) encounter a series of crises that set the stage for a larger, existential catastrophe.

title: Top 10 Reasons We Love the Original ‘Devil Wears Prada’ Movie
partialText: The 2006 comedy is filled with moments big and small that have stood the test of time, thanks in no small part to Meryl Streep’s turn as Miranda Priestly.

title: High-Profile Squatting Incidents Are on the Rise Across the Country

title: Crop Undercount Raises Questions About Reliability of U.S.D.A. Data
partialText: Corn estimates were off by 4.5 million acres last year. A lack of survey responses, not job cuts, led to the miss, the Agriculture Department said.

title: The Vaccine Skeptic in Trump’s New C.D.C. Leadership Team

title: Attacks on Jewish Targets in Europe Suggest Hybrid Warfare

title: Is Yoko Ono the Most Radical Artist of the Trump Era?

title: Smog in Phoenix and Salt Lake City? The E.P.A. Is Blaming Asia.
partialText: The Trump administration says the cities shouldn’t be penalized for unhealthy air because pollution can blow in from abroad. Some experts say that’s preposterous.

title: Forest Service Research Labs Are Closing
partialText: A research lab in Washington State tracks ecological changes in a warming climate and provides scientific guidance for forest managers. It is one of 57 such facilities being shuttered.

title: Minimal Comfort Feeding Is a New, Controversial Approach in Late Dementia
partialText: Some consider the regular feeding of late-stage dementia patients to be nonnegotiable. Others see it as extending life unnecessarily.

title: British Royals Crisscross Manhattan in Brief Visit Packed With Photo Ops

title: What the Royal State Dinner Guest List Says About Trump’s America
partialText: There were at least 10 American billionaires, six Fox News hosts, assorted presidential pals, no Democratic politicians and not so many British.

title: Mamdani Suggested UK Should Return the Koh-i-Noor Diamond. Here’s the Back Story.
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York suggested that Britain should return the gem, a symbol of colonial plunder. Here’s the back story of the famed jewel.

title: Mariah Explains Her Hit-Producing Songwriting Process

title: A Way to Slow Down ‘Super-Speeders’ Who Keep Breaking the Law
partialText: City and state officials want speed-limiting devices installed in the cars of drivers who get more than 16 speeding tickets in a year, in hopes of preventing injuries and deaths.

title: David Allan Coe, Singer Who Personified Outlaw Country, Dies at 86
partialText: Mr. Coe, who wrote “Take This Job and Shove It” and other hits, was a transgressive exponent of the outlaw country movement of the 1970s and ’80s.
